$comment: Generated API clients: which OpenAPI document each is typed from, and where
its output goes. Adding a client is a data edit, not a new script.
The document supplies the shape of each operation. The resolved deployment
graph supplies who may call it — see docs/adr/0023-generated-api-clients.md.
The two cannot be collapsed: `x-voyant-key-kind` is stamped at composition
time and appears in none of the tracked documents.
`keyKinds` is false for admin clients. The PK/SK line is a property of the
public surface; every /v1/admin/* route is secret-only by construction, so a
publishable subset there would be an empty type pretending to be a boundary.
`compose` merges a surface's documents into one, so the client is keyed by
URL instead of by package. The public surface is composed and admin is not,
and the asymmetry is deliberate:
- Documents move and URLs do not. voyant#4627 relocated the Trip-selection
routes between packages without changing a URL. Per-package subpaths on a
PUBLISHED client would make every such move a breaking change nobody
outside the repository can explain.
- A storefront consumes one surface with one credential; splitting it by
which package happens to serve a route leaks our layout into their code.
- Admin is 60 documents and ~1,100 paths, server-only, and its callers know
the domain they want. That is where paying only for what you import is
real. For 138 erased types it is not.
